newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end higher but worries linger.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end higher but worries linger.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures were propped by a stronger dollar/yen by the close of Friday trade but dealers said worries about Japan's banking and corporate sectors would continue to depress the market in the near term.
The lead Nikkei 225 September contract added 65 points to end at 19,830, 50 points below its day high.

Dealers said worries about the financial health of construction firm Aoki Corp stoked fears about the sector after last week's news that general contractor Tokai Kogyo Co Ltd had decided to apply for court protection from its creditors.
Aoki Corp was scheduled to hold a news briefing at 0300 GMT.
"Aoki is said to have a similar asset-liability ratio as Tokai Kogyo and people are saying it could go the same way," a dealer at an Asian institution said.
He said such speculation also added to concerns about Japanese banks being burdened with more bad loans.
"If the Nikkei gets back above 20,000 and sustains those gains, we could go higher. But the short-term bias is a little more to the downside," he said.
He added the September Nikkei should trade a 19,600-20,100 range for the time being.
On Taiwan futures, the July MSCI contract ended down at 401.5 against Thursday's close at 401.6. Volume was 1,539 lots.
